question: Two successive discounts of 30% and 20% was offered on food items. A man paid ₹840 for the food item. The bill amount of food item (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net equivalent discount = A + B − (A × B) ÷ 100

⇒ Net discount = 30 + 20 − (30 × 20) ÷ 100 = 50 − 6 = 44%

Selling Price (SP) = 100% − 44% = 56% of Marked Price (MP)

⇒ 56% of Bill Amount = 840

⇒ Bill Amount = 840 × (100 ÷ 56) = 1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First discount (D₁) = 30%

Second discount (D₂) = 20%

Selling price (SP) = ₹840

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

 
 MP = ?
 
 
 Inter. Price
 
 
 SP = ₹840
 
 

 

 −30%

 

 

 −20%
 
 MP × 0.7 × 0.8 = SP

**Calculations:**

⇒ 840 = MP × (1 − 30/100) × (1 − 20/100)

⇒ 840 = MP × (70/100) × (80/100)

⇒ 840 = MP × (7/10) × (8/10)

⇒ 840 = MP × (56/100)

⇒ MP = (840 × 100) ÷ 56

⇒ MP = 1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is given by [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price and Selling Price

Selling Price (SP) is the price paid by the customer after deducting the discount from the initial Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is [x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100]%. For discounts, x and y are taken as negative values.
